headline: Thousands gather as Iran mourns Supreme Leader Khamenei and family
summary: The former Supreme Leader and several family members, including a 14-month-old granddaughter, were killed in attacks during the early stages of a conflict with the US and Israel.
details: Thousands of people gathered at the Imam Khomeini Grand Musalla in Tehran on Friday to pay their final respects to former Supreme Leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei and his family members.
According to state media, Khamenei and several relatives were killed on February 28 during attacks launched by the US and Israel at the start of a conflict with Iran.

The deceased family members include his son-in-law Mesbah-ol-Hoda Bagheri, eldest daughter Sayyedeh Bushra Hosseini Khamenei, daughter-in-law Zahra Haddad Adel, and his 14-month-old granddaughter, Zahra Mohammadi Golpayegani.

The coffins of the deceased, all draped in the Iranian national flag, were placed at the Grand Musalla for public viewing. A photograph of the 14-month-old granddaughter was displayed next to her small coffin.
Religious leaders from Afghanistan and Indonesia, along with people from various walks of life, were among the first to arrive at the mosque to pay tribute.
Bangladesh's Speaker Hafiz Uddin Ahmed has also expressed solidarity with Iran during this period of national mourning.
caption:
A 14-month-old granddaughter among the dead. Iran begins mass mourning for Supreme Leader Khamenei and his family.

Thousands of people gathered at the Imam Khomeini Grand Musalla in Tehran on Friday to pay their final respects to former Supreme Leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei and his family members.

According to state media, Khamenei and several relatives were killed on February 28 during attacks launched by the US and Israel at the start of a conflict with Iran.

The deceased family members include his son-in-law Mesbah-ol-Hoda Bagheri, eldest daughter Sayyedeh Bushra Hosseini Khamenei, daughter-in-law Zahra Haddad Adel, and his 14-month-old granddaughter, Zahra Mohammadi Golpayegani.

The coffins of the deceased, all draped in the Iranian national flag, were placed at the Grand Musalla for public viewing. A photograph of the 14-month-old granddaughter was displayed next to her small coffin.

Religious leaders from Afghanistan and Indonesia, along with people from various walks of life, were among the first to arrive at the mosque to pay tribute.

Bangladesh's Speaker Hafiz Uddin Ahmed has also expressed solidarity with Iran during this period of national mourning.

Source: Jamuna TV, Dhaka Tribune, Somoy News, The Daily Star, Prothom Alo

headline: PM to attend memorial service for July uprising victims this Saturday
summary: Chief Adviser Muhammad Yunus will join the event to honor those who lost their lives during the student-led movement.
details: A memorial service to honor the victims of the July uprising will be held this Saturday.
Chief Adviser Muhammad Yunus is expected to attend the event to pay tribute to those who died during the protests.
The gathering serves as a formal recognition of the sacrifices made by students and citizens during the movement that led to the change in government.
The event is part of a series of initiatives to remember the martyrs of the student-led mass uprising.
